data.name: Manan
data.gender_notes: Manan is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manan is a name of Sanskrit and Hindu origin that means 'Thinker, Scholar'. This name signifies an individual who is deeply engaged in the process of contemplation and reflection. Manan is a name for those who value wisdom and knowledge, and who strive to gain a deeper understanding of the world around them. The name Manan carries the meaning “Thinker, Scholar” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Manan usually hope their child will grow to embody thinker, scholar and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Manan is a name that signifies spiritual depth and intellectual curiosity. It is a name that reflects a person's innate desire to explore the mysteries of life and to gain a deeper understanding of the universe. Manan is a name for those who are driven by their intellect and who seek to use their knowledge to make a positive impact on the world.
data.etymology: Manan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Thinker, Scholar.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manan total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Manan the Sage, also known as Manu Smriti, was a lawgiver and the author of the ancient Indian legal text, the Manusmriti. The text is one of the most authoritative texts in Hinduism, and is considered a foundational text in Hindu law. The Manusmriti is believed to have been written around the 2nd century BC.
historical_references.context: Author of Manusmriti, ancient Indian legal text

historical_references.reference: Manan is also the name of a famous Hindu king, Mananavarman, who ruled over the Chettinad region in present-day Tamil Nadu, India. He is known for his patronage of Jainism and his role in the spread of Jainism in South India. Mananavarman is believed to have ruled from the 11th to the 12th century AD.
historical_references.context: Famous Hindu king, patron of Jainism
